A drumbeat, not a trophy shelf.

Outlet screenshots and dated clips, newest first. Independent reporting, long conversations, business coverage, public-interest debate, and the occasional gloriously strange corner of the internet. The older web is still here. It just does not get the first screen.

Right now

The newest three stories show where the work is landing right now: building B.C.’s AI ecosystem across professions, public AI infrastructure as heavy industry, and the future of professional work.

Business in Vancouver / July 31, 2026

B.C. groups push to build a stronger AI ecosystem

Kris’s line lands in print: AI arrives inside every profession, not just inside an AI sector—and the province needs recurring rooms across those boundaries.

Daisy Xiong places BC + AI beside AInBC and the Economy of Wisdom Foundation in the provincial business conversation.

Coverage screenshot: BIV. Article photo: Rob Kruyt / BIV.
The Tyee / July 24, 2026

‘We Want a Role’: Who Gets a Say in AI Adoption?

Non-partisan framing of AI infrastructure as heavy industry, public bargaining, and consultation that can change outcomes.

Coverage screenshot: The Tyee.
Business in Vancouver / June 15, 2026

B.C. lawyers face AI-driven shakeups in legal work

Lead expert commentary on adoption, training, culture, and where human judgment still matters.

Coverage screenshot: BIV. Article photo: Rob Kruyt / BIV.
